newsitem.title: INDONESIA: More restructuring seen for Indonesia Salim Group.
newsitem.headline: More restructuring seen for Indonesia Salim Group.

text.p: Indonesia's Salim group is seen continuing to restructure its global operations after it proposed one of the largest takeovers in Singapore corporate history this week, analysts said on Wednesday.
They say the latest step in the ongoing restructuring of Indonesia's largest conglomerate is aimed at reducing risks and giving a further boost to its expansion plans.

"The Salim Group has been doing it for years. It is likely to continue doing so in a bid to reduce the risk of putting all the eggs in one basket," Beni Sindhunata, researcher with Indonesian Business Data Center, told Reuters.
The proposed restructuring involves the sale of a majority stake held by cement giant PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa in blue chip PT Indofood Sukses Makmur to Singapore's bread maker QAF Ltd.
Both Indocement and QAF are controlled by the Salim group.
"These efforts clearly demonstrate the group's desire to concentrate its core business into separate entities," Salim Group CEO Anthony Salim said in a statement issued on Tuesday.
Anthony Salim said the restructuring was another step in the Salim group's streamlining that began with the sale of Bogasari to Indofood in 1995 which involved about one trillion rupiah.
The move was followed by the acquisitions of six Salim companies by Indofood with a cost of 1.55 trillion rupiah in April this year.
In May, Salim said its Jakarta-based chemical unit PT Unggul Indah Corp planned to acquire a 100-percent stake in Singapore-based Salim Oleochemicals Pte Ltd, also a member of the Salim Group.
Salim said on Tuesday the plan to inject its flagship PT Indofood Sukses Makmur into bread maker QAF, would cost about 4.68 trillion rupiah.

"Other Indonesian conglomerates like the Sinar Mas Group through APP and Raja Garuda Mas through April have also done similar things by having listed companies abroad which have controlling stakes in Indonesian blue chips," another analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
New York-listed Sinar Mas' Asia Pulp and Paper Co Ltd, based in Singapore, has controlling stakes in Jakarta-listed paper giants PT Pabrik Kertas Tjiwi Kimia and PT Indah Kiat Pulp and Paper Corp.

Raja Garuda Mas' Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings, listed in New York, is also based in Singapore and has controlling stakes in Jakarta-listed pulp and rayon firm PT Inti Indorayon Utama.

Analysts said the continued move to diversify overseas was gaining further momentum partly because of the latest political developments particularly after the May general elections-related riots and ahead of the presidential election next March.
"You can't have all your companies based in Jakarta not just because of limitations of the local demand, but also partly because of political considerations," a foreign analyst said.

Analysts said they were watching for further restructuring involving other Salim entities, including Hong Kong's blue chip First Pacific Co Ltd which has global business interests including in China, Europe, India and the Philippines.
